subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable memory recall eligibility and index exclusion paths for markdown-first workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared configurable include/exclude path-scope contract for both memory-core recall eligibility and Memory Search indexing, and should it cover builtin and QMD backends now?
rationale: This adds compatibility-sensitive public config across memory recall, search indexing, and persisted index behavior, so automation should not choose the long-term API shape or backend parity boundary.

options.title: Add shared memory path scopes
options.body: Introduce one include/exclude evaluator used by memory-core recall and Memory Search indexing, with defaults preserving current behavior and tests covering diagnostics, sync, and reindex identity.

options.title: Land builtin search exclusion first
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95739 or a successor as a narrow first step and leave recall eligibility and QMD parity explicitly tracked here.

options.title: Defer to memory plugin convergence
options.body: Keep the request open until the memory plugin convergence work defines the path-scope contract with broader memory architecture decisions.

recommendation.title: Add shared memory path scopes
recommendation.body: Introduce one include/exclude evaluator used by memory-core recall and Memory Search indexing, with defaults preserving current behavior and tests covering diagnostics, sync, and reindex identity.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory host SDK and QMD extraPaths history makes vincentkoc the strongest routing candidate for the config/API shape decision.
